styrkan ligger i öppenheten: två vittnen och fyra kontroller, redovisade för varje sten, så att den som vet mer kan se exakt var resonemanget brister. - planen för provet skrevs och låstes 2026-10-21, innan blindprovet räknades (sha-256 5ed0b2f3b147…; metoddokumentationen avsnitt 1x och 14c). - underlag: vikingatida runstenar i samnordisk runtextdatabas 3.1, korpusversion 5fdfd1e095bfb6fb. stenöversiktens regel är oförändrad: nytt förslag vid en styrka på minst 0,5, möjligt vid minst 0,3, och modellens kanske någon annan när förstavalet får under 35 procent. - blindprovet: 769 stenar med säker ristare. attribueringen doldes och ristarnas landskap räknades om utan stenen; modellens sannolikheter är korsvaliderade, alltså hämtade från modeller som inte såg stenen. en oberoende omräkning av 60 slumpvis valda stenar gav exakt samma resultat. - jämförelsen: ristaren bakom den närmaste andra stenen med säker ristare; står flera lika nära räknas alla deras ristare. mcnemars avstånd efter den första körningen, vilket höjde dess träff från 41 till 44 procent och gör jämförelsen svårare för vitki. planen sa att de tio starkaste skulle visas med alla belägg; här visas fem i detalj och fem i tabell, och alla belägg finns i appen. träffsäkerheten per ristare och per landskap är tillägg utöver planen. se själv öppna stenöversikt i vitki, stäng av alla statusar utom nytt förslag och välj visa som tabell. klicka på en sten för att se vad varje metod säger om den. modellen och dess kanske någon annan finns under statistik → vem ristade?. blindprovets alla rader finns i posts.text_en: we now want to show one of vitki's real strengths. of the 2,321 swedish viking-age runestones in the scandinavian runic-text database (rundata), 1,550 have no carver – two out of three. no one recorded who cut them, and for most of them we will never know. but the stones carry traces of their carvers: how the words are spelled, which signs separate them, the ornament, the place. these are the traces runologists follow when they attribute a stone by hand, one at a time. vitki follows them for all the stones at once and says, for each stone, whether the evidence points to one of the carvers vitki knows – and how strongly. it shows in the stone overview. there 86 stones without a carver get a new suggestion, which means that the evidence points strongly to a carver. another 292 get a possible suggestion. for the rest, 1,172 stones, the evidence is not enough for any suggestion at all. the stone overview's chart of the stones without a carver the stone overview in vitki: every dot is a runestone without a carver in rundata, and the further right, the more strongly the evidence points to a carver. dark blue is a new suggestion (strength at least 0.5), light blue a possible suggestion (at least 0.3). screenshot from vitki. a suggestion is only worth something if we know how often it is right. so we do not begin with the suggestions but with a test. first a blind test rundata gives a certain carver for 769 runestones. we let vitki go through them one at a time with the answer hidden. the carver was removed from the stone's record, and everything vitki knows about the carvers – where they worked, which style groups and rock types they used, how they spelled – was recounted without that stone. then vitki had its say, exactly as if the stone had never had a carver. how the test would be run and what would count as success we wrote down and locked before we saw a single result. as the opponent we chose the simplest rule we could think of: guess the carver behind the nearest stone with a known carver. the rule is not stupid. carvers worked in their home districts, and the neighbouring stone often has the same carver. when vitki gave a new suggestion it was rundata's carver in 248 of 302 cases, 82 per cent – probably somewhere between 77 and 86 per cent. the nearest-carver rule was right on the same stones in 44 per cent of cases. most telling are the stones where the two disagree: on 132 vitki was right and the rule wrong, on 17 it was the other way round. if vitki and the rule were equally good, a split that lopsided would almost never arise by chance (p ≈ 3 · 10⁻²³). that is less likely than winning the top prize in the lottery three weeks in a row. the hardest test is the 100 signed stones among them. there the carver's name stands on the stone, so the key does not rest on any scholar's judgement of style or spelling. vitki was right on 72 of them, the rule on 42. even the weaker possible suggestions beat the rule, 55 against 34 per cent. and the stronger the suggestion, the more often it holds: with a strength of at least 0.7 vitki was right in 86 per cent of cases, 142 of 165. how vitki reasons how does vitki arrive at a suggestion? take u 843 from hässle in dalby parish outside uppsala. the stone is lost, and we know it from a drawing made before 1693. according to the inscription four people had it raised in memory of their father ulfr. rundata gives no carver. the runestone u 843 u 843 at hässle in dalby parish, drawn before 1693. the stone is lost. drawing: johan hadorph och sven bierkenius, cc0, via wikimedia commons. vitki lets two witnesses speak and then tests their evidence against four checks. the first witness is a statistical model in r, a so-called random forest, which has learned to recognise 18 carvers on 497 stones with a known carver. it weighs together where the stone stands, ornament, crosses, spelling, word dividers, formulas and content. for u 843 the model says fótr – fot 2 in rundata – with 72 per cent. the model is cautious by nature. when it was tested on stones it had not been allowed to see, it said at least 70 per cent about 20 stones and was right about all 20. the second witness is the spelling. vitki compares the stone's text, with the names removed, with how each carver usually spells and places word dividers. u 843 most resembles fótr's stones. when the spelling puts fótr first it has been right 36 times out of 56, just under two times in three. since the text has only 8 words the witness is discounted further, to 0.45. then the witnesses are weighed together. both can be wrong: the model in 28 per cent of cases, the spelling in 55. both being wrong at the same time, if they are independent of each other, happens in 28 per cent of 55 per cent of cases, that is about 16 per cent. that gives the strength 0.84. last come the checks: do the area, the style group, the language traits and the rock type agree with the carver's other stones? every check that speaks against lowers the strength, down to half if all speak against. for u 843 one of fótr's stones, u 841 at dalby church, stands a kilometre away. style group and rock type cannot be tested for the lost stone. the language traits may only speak against, never for, since the spelling has already had its say. nothing speaks against, and the strength stays at 0.84. u 843 in the stone overview u 843 in the stone overview. the strength 0.84 comes from the model (0.72) and the spelling (0.45); of the checks only the area can be tested (om ✓). screenshot from vitki. the formula assumes that the witnesses are independent, and they are not entirely, because both look partly at the spelling. that is why the strength is an index for sorting the stones, not a probability. it is also why the blind test was needed: it shows what the index is worth. five stones here are the five strongest new suggestions. we have not chosen them by hand: they are the stone overview's five highest, by the rule in the locked plan. the top list in the stone overview the top list in the stone overview: every status except new suggestion switched off, the table sorted by the suggestion's strength. rundata and support are empty, since the stones have no carver in rundata. screenshot from vitki. three of the five concern traen, and that name needs an explanation. rundata gives 22 runestones in södermanland the carver traen, 12 of them in rönö hundred. but the name rests on a misreading (gustavson & snædal brink 1981, pp. 196–97; axelson 1993, p. 74), and bianchi (2010, pp. 153–55) and kitzler åhfeldt (2017, pp. 65–66) see the stones as the work of several carvers rather than one. so when vitki says traen it means that the stone belongs among these stones, in a local tradition – not that a person called traen cut it. 1. sö 62 at hässlö – the traen group, strength 0.88 the runestone sö 62 sö 62 at hässlö in lerbo parish, södermanland. gunni raised the stone at hässlö in lerbo parish in memory of his son ragni, who died on the way west. the model gives traen 52 per cent, and at that level it has been right nine times out of ten. the spelling also puts traen first, but only just ahead of tidkume, so that witness counts for somewhat less. the style group pr1 belongs to the core of the traen stones, and the nearest of them, sö 49 at ene, stands 24 kilometres away. one language trait speaks against: the stone writes rasti stan with a, where nearly all traen stones have ai, as in ræisti stæin. the form with a occurs on only 6 per cent of them, against 20 per cent in the province. the simple rule would have guessed steinkell, whose stone sö 54 stands nearest, 8 kilometres away. runor 2020 gives no carver. 2. sö 158 at österberga – the traen group, 0.87 the runestone sö 158 the ship on sö 158 at österberga in runtuna parish: the bind-runes form the mast. on sö 158 in runtuna parish, in the middle of the traen stones' district, a ship is carved. the bind-runes form the mast, and the name of the dead father, kitilhafþa, stands in the sail. runor 2020 notes that the stone was earlier read as signed by traen. in the reading rundata follows today, gustavson and snædal brink's from 1981, there is no signature: the bind-runes in the mast become instead a judgement on the father, þrottar þiagn, roughly “a thegn of strength”. that is why the stone has no carver in rundata. vitki knows nothing of that history; runor's notes are not part of the evidence. still the stone ends up among the traen stones. the model says traen with 68 per cent, a level at which it has been right 60 times out of 61, and the spelling puts traen first. the nearest traen stone, sö 153 at skarpåker, stands 1.5 kilometres away, and four of the group's stones stand in the same parish. bind-runes occur on 11 per cent of the traen stones against 5 per cent in the province. but there is a neighbour that complicates the picture. a kilometre away, also at österberga, stands sö 159, signed by gunnleifr, hrœríkr and guðmundr. that is the stone the simple rule would have guessed, and in the blind test vitki took that very stone for a traen stone. so vitki cannot separate the traen group from the three who signed the neighbouring stone. that is a question for someone who can compare the stones themselves – and it is exactly the kind of question vitki is good at asking. 3. u 1026 at lena church – œpir, 0.85 the runestone u 1026 u 1026 at lena church in uppland. at lena church in norunda hundred two stones stand on the same spot, u 1026 and u 1027. brandr and sigviðr had u 1026 raised in memory of their brother mundi, and rundata notes that the ornament in style group pr4 is skilfully designed. here only the model speaks, since the text becomes too short for the spelling comparison once the names are removed. but the model speaks clearly: œpir (öpir 1 in rundata), 85 per cent. that is the surest answer it gives for any of the 810 stones that have no carver at all in rundata. pr4 belongs to the core of œpir's stones, and the word divider that rundata renders with an apostrophe (') occurs on 55 per cent of œpir's stones against 11 per cent in uppland. the nearest œpir stones stand at tensta church, 4 kilometres away. the simple rule would have guessed ásmundr and vígmundr, whose stone u 1031 at hånsta stands 2 kilometres away. that stone vitki got right in the blind test: with the answer hidden, vitki suggested ásmundr. runor 2020 says that u 1026 and u 1027 have the same carver, without naming one. vitki gives both the same name: u 1027 gets œpir with the strength 0.74. since the stones stand on the same spot that is no strong test, but different names would have been a warning. one more reservation: œpir is the name vitki reaches for most often. when vitki has suggested œpir in the blind test it has held 68 times out of 104, the worst of all carvers vitki has suggested more than three times. probabilities as high as 85 per cent, however, the model has not yet got wrong when tested. 4. u 843 at hässle – fótr, 0.84 u 843 we have already followed through the machinery. what makes the suggestion strong is that two witnesses looking at different things – the model at the whole, the spelling at the text – point to the same carver. the divider × occurs on 73 per cent of fótr's stones against 15 per cent in uppland, and auk for “and” on 95 per cent against 52. here the simple rule would have guessed the same, but by a narrow margin: fótr's stone at dalby church stands 15 metres closer than a stone by œpir at the same church. another of fótr's stones, u 844 at viggeby bridge, got the right suggestion in the blind test. runor 2020 gives no carver, and for the lost stone there is only the drawing to examine. 5. sö 72 at kesäter – the traen group, 0.83, and the list's weakest link sö 72 in västra vingåker parish is also lost. ulfr and a person whose name cannot be interpreted raised the stone in memory of styrmaðr, and the inscription ends with a prayer: may god help their souls. here only the spelling speaks. the model does not answer at all, since the stone stands more than 25 kilometres from every stone it was trained on. the spelling puts traen first, and when it does it has been right 14 times out of 16. hence the high figure. still the suggestion is the list's weakest, for three reasons. the nearest traen stone, sö 112 at kolunda, stands 46 kilometres away, far from the group's core. one language trait speaks against: the stone has iftir (after), where the traen stones mostly write at; the form æftir occurs on only 15 per cent of them against 42 per cent in the province. and the blind test can say nothing about suggestions of this kind, since no stone in the test got a new suggestion on the spelling alone. sö 72 is a suggestion to test, not to trust. the next five - u 482 at kasby – fot, strength 0.82 (the model 0.67, the spelling 0.45). runor 2020: no carver. - sö 70 at hedenlunda – traen-gruppen, strength 0.79 (the model 0.49, the spelling 0.58). runor 2020: no carver. - sö 137 at aspa – traen-gruppen, strength 0.79 (the model 0.41, the spelling 0.63). runor 2020: no carver. - u 136 at broby – fot, strength 0.78 (the model 0.39, the spelling 0.64). runor 2020: same carver as u 135. - sö 335 at ärja ödekyrka – traen-gruppen, strength 0.75 (the model 0.40, the spelling 0.58). runor 2020: no carver. two stones stronger than sö 335, u 854 and u 957, are not included, because the model says perhaps someone else about them: none of its carvers reaches 35 per cent. that applies to 17 of the 86 new suggestions. u 136 at broby has, according to runor 2020, the same carver as the neighbouring stone u 135, and vitki gives both fótr. the same holds for u 297 and u fv1979;245 at skånela church. in all three pairs where runor says that two nameless stones have the same carver and both get a new suggestion, vitki gives them the same name. for sö 137 at aspa there are also measurements of the carving technique: kitzler åhfeldt (2017, pp. 41–46) places it in a different technique group from the traen stone sö 164 – another sign that the traen group holds several hands. in all, 30 of the 86 new suggestions concern œpir, 18 fótr, 15 the traen group and 14 balli. of them 65 stand in uppland, 20 in södermanland and one in västmanland. none of them is contradicted by runor 2020 – but mostly because runor gives no carver for them either. only for u 1015 does runor already give a carver, and it is the same one vitki suggests: œpir. what vitki cannot do vitki only knows carvers with enough stones to learn from: 18 in the model and 27 in the spelling comparison, 28 in all, nearly all active in uppland and södermanland. a stone by someone else can still get one of their names. in the blind test 133 of the 769 stones were carved by someone vitki does not know, and 23 of them still got a new suggestion. they cannot be right, and they are counted in the 82 per cent. the model can now say perhaps someone else when none of its carvers fits, but it also warns unnecessarily. the model's perhaps someone else statistics → who carved? in vitki: when none of the model's carvers reaches 35 per cent it says perhaps someone else. screenshot from vitki. nor is the key independent. in uppland and södermanland rundata's attributions rest largely on axelson's list from 1993 and on earlier scholars' judgements of style and spelling – the same kind of traces vitki follows. that is why the signed stones are the most important test. södermanland is vitki's weaker province. there new suggestions were right in 17 of 28 cases (61 per cent), against 46 per cent for the simple rule, and with so few stones that difference may be chance. three of the five strongest suggestions concern södermanland. when vitki has suggested traen it has held 11 times out of 15, and all four misses were stones that other carvers in the province signed, among them sö 159 at österberga. that fits the picture of the traen group as a local tradition rather than a hand. of the 86 suggestions, 18 concern lost stones. their text and ornament we know only from older drawings and readings, and an error there follows into the evidence. a test against runor 2020 was too small to say anything. runor gives carvers for 19 runestones that have no carver in rundata 3.1, but only eight of them have a carver vitki knows, and none of them got a new suggestion. of three possible suggestions, one held. what it gives us a model like this cannot give us new attributions. only someone who examines the stones can. but it gives runology something that is hard to produce by hand: a work list of all sweden's runestones without a carver, ordered by how strongly the evidence points, with every piece of evidence visible. it shows where scholarship's own groups hold together in the data, as when sö 158, once read as signed by traen, lands among the traen stones without vitki knowing of that reading. it finds the places where the question is open, such as österberga. and it can say how often it is right: four times out of five, in a test where the answer was hidden. - vitki does for all runestones at once what runologists have done by hand, one stone at a time, and can also say how often it holds: in a blind test with the answer hidden, the new suggestions were right four times out of five, about twice as often as a guess at the nearest known carver. - the five strongest suggestions are hypotheses to test against the stones – ornament, rune forms and carving technique – not new attributions. the weakest, sö 72, rests on the spelling alone. - traen is not a person but a group of stones with a misread name. a traen suggestion places a stone in a local tradition in södermanland, where vitki is also at its least certain. - the strength lies in the openness: two witnesses and four checks, reported for every stone, so that anyone who knows more can see exactly where the reasoning falls short. - the plan for the test was written and locked on 21 october 2026, before the blind test was computed (sha-256 5ed0b2f3b147…; the methods documentation, sections 1x and 14c). - data: viking-age runestones in the scandinavian runic-text database 3.1, corpus version 5fdfd1e095bfb6fb. the stone overview's rule is unchanged: new suggestion at a strength of at least 0.5, possible at at least 0.3, and the model's perhaps someone else when the first choice gets under 35 per cent. - the blind test: 769 stones with a certain carver. the attribution was hidden and the carvers' provinces recounted without the stone; the model's probabilities are cross-validated, that is taken from models that did not see the stone. an independent recomputation of 60 randomly chosen stones gave exactly the same result. - the comparison: the carver behind the nearest other stone with a certain carver; if several stand equally near, all their carvers count. mcnemar's exact test on the stones where vitki and the rule disagree, and wilson's 95 per cent intervals. - deviations from the plan: the r module cut the list of the model's suggestions to 400 stones. the fault was corrected after the first run, which gave a new corpus version and 86 instead of 79 new suggestions; the precision was 82 per cent both before and after. the nearest-carver rule was made generous at equal distances after the first run, which raised its hit rate from 41 to 44 per cent and makes the comparison harder for vitki. the plan said the ten strongest would be shown with all their evidence; here five are shown in detail and five in a list, and all the evidence is in the app. the hit rates per carver and per province are additions beyond the plan. see for yourself open the stone overview in vitki, switch off every status except new suggestion and choose show as table. click a stone to see what each method says about it. the model and its perhaps someone else are under statistics → who carved?. all the rows of the blind test are in vitki's open source code. sources - axelson, j. 1993. mellansvenska runristare. förteckning över signerade och attribuerade inskrifter. runrön 5. uppsala. - bianchi, m. 2010. runor som resurs. vikingatida skriftkultur i uppland och södermanland. runrön 20. uppsala. - gustavson, h. & snædal brink, t. 1981. runfynd 1980. fornvännen 76: 186–202. - kitzler åhfeldt, l. 2017. runristare och mobilitet i södermanland. stockholm. - runor. swedish national heritage board, 2020 edition. - scandinavian runic-text database, version 3.1 (odbl). - images: see the captions.
posts.summary: två av tre svenska runstenar saknar ristare i rundata. vitki går igenom alla och säger var beläggen pekar – och i ett blindprov på 769 stenar, där svaret var dolt, hade de nya förslagen rätt fyra gånger av fem. här är de fem starkaste, och hur vitki kommer fram till dem.
posts.summary_en: two of three swedish runestones have no carver in rundata. vitki goes through them all and says where the evidence points – and in a blind test on 769 stones, with the answer hidden, the new suggestions were right four times out of five. here are the five strongest, and how vitki arrives at them.

posts.title: Stenar och stavar – sex betydelser av ett runord
posts.title_en: Stones and staves – six meanings of a runic word
posts.text: aspastenen sö 137 i vitkis 3d-verktyg aspastenen (sö 137) i södermanland, stenens andra sida, i strykljus ur en 3d-skanning. i de två övre raderna går runornas huvudstavar tvärs över bandet. i den nedersta raden är många runor bara korta snedstreck: det är stavlösa runor. bilden är beräknad i vitki ur laila kitzler åhfeldts skanning (riksantikvarieämbetet, cc by 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.11951255). den som läser om runor stöter snart på ordet stav. runologen skriver att ”bistaven” är skadad, eddan talar om ”stora stavar”, och på runstenarna själva står att någon ”reste stavar och stenar”. det är inte samma sak. här är ordets sex betydelser, med det som stenarna själva säger om dem. - runans delar. en runa byggs av en huvudstav och bistavar. det är bistavarna som skiljer runorna åt. - runan själv. på fornnordiska heter ett skrivtecken stafr. två runstenar kallar sina egna runor för stavar. - ett minnesmärke. fem vikingatida inskrifter, kanske sex, alla i mälardalen, säger att en staf restes tillsammans med stenen. ingen av stavarna finns kvar. tre av de fem talar om flera stenar, mot en av trettio bland alla andra runstenar, och två hör till ett monument som nämner ett ting. - stavlösa runor. en snabbskrift där huvudstavarna nästan saknas, bland annat i den nedersta raden på aspastenen. - runstaven och primstaven. kalendrar av trä, och på gotländska gravhällar ett tal i påsktabellen. - galdrastavar och stavrim. isländska trolltecken, mycket yngre än vikingatiden, och versens bokstavsrim. 1. huvudstaven och bistavarna en runa i den yngre runraden byggs nästan alltid kring ett lodrätt streck, huvudstaven. ut från den, eller tvärs över den, går kortare streck: bistavarna. runan i är bara en huvudstav. lägger man till en bistav snett över mitten blir den a eller n, beroende på åt vilket håll bistaven lutar. en bistav uppåt höger från mitten gör en k-runa, två bistavar som sluttar ner från toppen gör ett t. huvudstav och bistav sex runor ur den yngre runraden med huvudstaven i svart och bistavarna i rost. längst till höger det som finns kvar i ett hål på en runsten i vada kyrka i uppland: en böjd bistav men ingen huvudstav. figur: vitki. därför är bistavarna det runologen tittar efter först. i de två häften av södermanlands runinskrifter (1924–36) som vi har som text skriver erik brate och elias wessén ”bst”, bistav, minst 218 gånger och ”hst”, huvudstav, 143 gånger. bistaven nämns oftare eftersom det är den som avgör vilken runa det är. när bara huvudstaven finns kvar kan runan vara nästan vad som helst. två exempel visar hur det låter när en runa är skadad: - om en gravhäll i strängnäs (sö 280) skriver brate och wessén: ”nedre delen av en stav, som lutar svagt åt vänster; snarast u, möjligen r”. bara huvudstaven syns, och då står valet mellan flera runor. - om ett fragment i vada kyrka skriver magnus källström 2011: ”en svagt bågböjd bistav till k”, och att runan också kan ha varit f. här är det tvärtom: bistaven syns, men huvudstaven är borta. 2. stav betyder runa på fornnordiska heter ett skrivtecken stafr, i plural stafir. i eddadikten hávamál, strof 142, får läsaren rådet: > rúnar munt þú finna ok ráðna stafi, mjǫk stóra stafi, mjǫk stinna stafi … > ”runor ska du finna och tydbara stavar, mycket stora stavar, mycket starka stavar …” samma ordpar, runor och stavar, står på runstenarna. på nöbbelestenen i småland (sm 16) ska den döde minnas ”medan stenen och runstavarna lever”, meðan stæinn lifir ok stafir runa. på randbølstenen i jylland (dr 40) står: ”mycket länge ska dessa stavar leva för torgunn.” långt senare, på en medeltida norsk ristning (n 13), skriver áslakr: rúnar ek ríst ok ráðna stafi, ”runor ristar jag och tydbara stavar” – nästan ordagrant som i hávamál. ordet lever kvar i vårt bokstav. om förleden från början syftade på boken eller på trädet boken, som man kunde rista i, är omstritt. 3. stavarna som stod bredvid stenarna den mest gåtfulla betydelsen finns på fem runstenar, kanske sex. där är staf inte ett tecken utan ett minnesmärke, rest tillsammans med stenen: - vreta i uppland (u 332): ”inga reste staven och stenarna efter ragnfast, sin make.” - stora rytterne i västmanland (vs 1): ”gudlev satte staven och dessa stenar efter slagve, sin son, som dog i öster.” - bällsta i uppland (u 226): ”de reste stenarna och gjorde(?) också staven, den stora, som hedersminne.” - balingsta i uppland (u 849): ”igull och hauk gjorde staven, och nase och anund reste stenen.” - kolsundet vid husby i södermanland (sö 196): ”ingefrid lät resa denna sten och stav efter öjulv, sin fader.” - fyrby i södermanland (sö 56), ristad på ett jordfast block: de mest runkunniga bröderna i midgård ”satte sten och många stavar” efter sin fader. här är forskarna oeniga: stafa marga kan också betyda runorna i texten. inte en enda av stavarna finns kvar. stenarna har överlevt i tusen år, stavarna har försvunnit helt. det tyder på att de var av trä, men hur de såg ut, om de var ristade eller målade, vet vi inte. ordet har ytterligare en betydelse på forsaringen i hälsingland (hs 7), en järnring med runor från 800-talet. där ska böterna betalas ”till staven”. enligt rundatas översättning gäller det återställandet av en helgedom. staven är då något i rätten eller kulten, inte ett minnesmärke. vad forskningen säger vi har hittat lite skrivet om stavarna. kristel zilmer delar i sin avhandling från 2005 upp ställena i två grupper: där staf betyder runorna (sm 16, dr 40 och möjligen sö 56) och där en stav reses som minnesmärke (de fem ovan). tomáš vlasatý i projekt forlǫg har jämfört stavarna med en samtida ögonvittnesskildring. omkring år 922 såg den arabiske diplomaten ibn fadlan en hövdings begravning hos ett folk han kallade rus, vid volga. när skeppet hade bränts, skriver han, byggde de ”något som liknade en rund kulle över skeppet … och satte i mitten av den en stor bit björk, på vilken de skrev mannens namn och namnet på rus kung”. vlasatý menar att trästolpar kan ha varit ett billigare alternativ till stenar, som höll i högst omkring hundra år. det är hans förslag. men skildringen visar att en trästolpe med skrift kunde vara ett minnesmärke vid den här tiden. någon utgrävning där en sådan stav har hittats vid en runsten har vi inte funnit. vad stenarna med stavar har gemensamt vi jämförde de fem stenarna med en säker stav med alla andra vikingatida runstenar i samnordisk runtextdatabas, också fragment och försvunna stenar, i statistikprogrammet r: två saker sticker ut: - stavarna står i monument med flera stenar. tre av de fem talar om ”staven och stenarna”. bland alla andra runstenar talar bara en av trettio om flera stenar. med fem stenar kunde slumpen ge en träff, knappast tre. sannolikheten att få ett så stort utslag av en slump är 0,002, även när vi räknar med att vi gjorde sju test. - två av monumenten hör ihop med ett ting. på bällsta står på systerstenen u 225 att sönerna ”gjorde här en tingsplats”, och på kolsundet (sö 196) nämns ett ting, i en osäker läsning. bland alla andra runstenar nämner bara 9 av 2 625 ett ting. det mönstret såg vi när vi läste texterna, och testet gjordes efteråt. det är därför ett fynd att pröva vidare, inte ett bevis. de andra skillnaderna pekar åt samma håll men kan vara slump, eftersom stenarna är så få. stavarna hör till den tidiga delen av runstenstiden: tre av de fyra som har en stilgrupp är huggna i rak, fp eller pr1, ungefär 980–1050, och mittåret är 1030 mot 1060 för de andra stenarna i mälardalen (sannolikheten för slump är 0,070, och 0,28 efter justeringen för sju test). alla fem står i mälardalen, där tre av fem runstenar finns. två av fem är signerade av en ristare, mot ungefär var tionde annars. sammantaget nämns stavarna i stora, offentliga monument med flera stenar, ibland vid en tingsplats och oftast tidigt. det är vad siffrorna visar. vad stavarna var vet vi fortfarande inte. - 800-talet: forsaringen (hs 7), stav i rättslig mening. - omkring 980–1015 (stilgruppen rak): runorna kallas stavar (sm 16, dr 40), och bröderna på fyrby sätter ”många stavar” (sö 56). - omkring 1010–1075 (fp–pr3): stavar reses som minnesmärken (sö 196, u 226, vs 1, u 332). - medeltiden: rúnar ek ríst ok ráðna stafi (n 13), och primstaven på sju gotländska inskrifter 1324–1553. 4. stavlösa runor på några stenar har ristaren nästan helt tagit bort huvudstavarna. kvar blir bistavarna och korta stumpar av staven, en sorts snabbskrift. de kallas stavlösa runor eller, efter det landskap där de främst finns, hälsingerunor. det mest kända exemplet är malstastenen i hälsingland (hs 14). de förekommer också i södermanland. om aspastenen (sö 137) skriver riksantikvarieämbetets databas runor: ”sista raden med stavlösa runor förutom sista ordet”. bilden överst i artikeln visar skillnaden. i de övre raderna står huvudstavarna som höga streck över hela bandet, i den nedersta raden är många runor bara korta snedstreck. 5. runstaven och primstaven en runstav är en kalender, oftast ristad på en träkäpp, där runor och tecken markerar årets dagar och högtider. den användes från medeltiden och på sina håll in på 1700-talet. ett annat ord för den är primstav, efter primtalet, det tal som anger var i den nittonåriga månkretsen ett år hamnar och som behövs för att räkna ut påsken. ordet finns på sju medeltida inskrifter på gotland från 1324 till 1553, de flesta på gravhällar: g 12, g 55, g 78, g 124, g 182, g 306, g 308. de anger året genom söndagsbokstaven och ”primstaven” i påsktabellen. på hällen i hemse kyrka (g 55) från 1459 står till exempel att hagal var söndagsbokstav det året, och att primstaven var den ”i tolfte raden i tabellen”. 6. galdrastavar och stavrim galdrastavar (galdrastafir) är isländska trolltecken från handskrifter från 1500-talet och framåt, till exempel vegvísir. de kallas ibland runor, men de är egna tecken och många hundra år yngre än runstenarna. stavrim är bokstavsrimmet i den fornnordiska versen: ord som börjar med samma ljud binder ihop raden. nöbbelestenens formel ovan är ett exempel: meðan stæinn lifir ok stafir runa. stenen och stavarna rimmar på varandra. så gjorde vi - runstenarnas egna ord: alla normaliseringar i samnordisk runtextdatabas (version 3.1, 2018) som innehåller staf-, med rundatas översättningar. ord som stafn, ”stäv”, är borträknade. - stavlösa runor: anteckningarna i riksantikvarieämbetets databas runor (2020). - huvudstav och bistav: förkortningarna ”hst” och ”bst” räknade i de två häften av södermanlands runinskrifter som vi har som text. texten är maskinläst, så några förekomster kan ha fallit bort. - statistiken om stavarna: de fem stenarna med en säker stav jämfördes med alla andra vikingatida runstenar, också fragment och försvunna stenar, med fishers exakta test. inskrifter på gravhällar, berghällar och lösa föremål som mynt och runpinnar är inte med. fishers test passar när en grupp är så liten. vi gjorde sju test, och p-värdena är justerade för det (holms metod). ”flera stenar” betyder att texten har stæina, stæinar eller stæinum; ”ting” att den har þing, där bällsta räknas som ett monument (u 225 och u 226). ting-testet gjordes efter att vi sett mönstret. skripten är scripts/stavar data.py och scripts/stavar stats.r. - bilden av aspastenen: strykljus från nordväst, beräknat i vitki ur den öppna 3d-skanningen. bilderna kommer från vitki, ett öppet verktyg för runstensforskning som du kan ladda ner och köra på din egen dator från github. källor - samnordisk runtextdatabas (rundata), institutionen för nordiska språk, uppsala universitet. open database license. - runor, riksantikvarieämbetet, utgåva 2020 av samnordisk runtextdatabas. - brate, e. & wessén, e. 1924–36. södermanlands runinskrifter (sveriges runinskrifter 3). stockholm: kvhaa. digitaliserad av riksantikvarieämbetet. - källström, m. 2011. u fv1971;212b vada kyrka. ett digitalt supplement till upplands runinskrifter, version 0.1. riksantikvarieämbetet. - hávamál, strof 142, i guðni jónssons utgåva av eddan (heimskringla.no). översättningen är vår. - ibn fadlan, risala, i james e. montgomerys översättning: ibn faḍlān and the rūsiyyah. journal of arabic and islamic studies 3, 2000, s. 1–25. vår svenska översättning efter den engelska. - vlasatý, t. 2022. „þorbjǫrn the skald carved the runes“. projekt forlǫg. - zilmer, k. 2005. ”he drowned in holmr's sea – his cargo-ship drifted to the sea-bottom, only three came out alive”: records and representations of baltic traffic in the viking age and the early middle ages in early nordic sources. tartu: tartu university press, s. 156. - kitzler åhfeldt, l. 2024. 3d-data runstenar i södermanland [dataset]. riksantikvarieämbetet. doi:10.5281/zenodo.11951255. cc by 4.0.
posts.text_en: the aspa stone sö 137 in vitki's 3d tool the aspa stone (sö 137) in södermanland, the stone's other side, in raking light from a 3d scan. in the two upper rows the runes' main staves run across the whole band. in the bottom row many runes are only short slanting strokes: these are staveless runes. the image was computed in vitki from laila kitzler åhfeldt's scan (swedish national heritage board, cc by 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.11951255). anyone who reads about runes soon meets the word stave. the runologist writes that the "branch" is damaged, the edda speaks of "great staves", and the runestones themselves say that someone "raised staves and stones". these are not the same thing. here are the word's six meanings, with what the stones themselves say about them. - the parts of a rune. a rune is built from a main staff and branches. it is the branches that tell the runes apart. - the rune itself. in old norse a written character is a stafr. two runestones call their own runes staves. - a monument. five viking-age inscriptions, perhaps six, all in the mälaren valley, say that a staf was raised together with the stone. none of the staves survives. three of the five speak of several stones, against one in thirty of all other runestones, and two belong to a monument that mentions an assembly. - staveless runes. a shorthand in which the main staves are almost gone, among other places in the bottom row of the aspa stone. - the rune staff and the prime staff. calendars of wood, and on gotlandic grave slabs a number in the easter table. - magic staves and alliteration. icelandic magical signs, much younger than the viking age, and the rhyming of initial sounds in verse. 1. the main staff and the branches a rune of the younger futhark is almost always built around a vertical line, the main staff. from it, or across it, run shorter strokes: the branches. the rune i is only a main staff. add a branch slanting across the middle and it becomes a or n, depending on which way the branch leans. a branch rising to the right from the middle makes a k-rune; two branches sloping down from the top make a t. main staff and branch six runes of the younger futhark with the main staff in black and the branches in rust. on the far right, what remains in a hole on a runestone in vada church in uppland: a curved branch but no main staff. figure: vitki. that is why the branches are what the runologist looks for first. in the two parts of södermanlands runinskrifter (1924–36) that we have as text, erik brate and elias wessén write "bst", branch, at least 218 times and "hst", main staff, 143 times. the branch is mentioned more often because it is what decides which rune it is. when only the main staff is left, the rune could be almost anything. two examples show how it sounds when a rune is damaged: - of a grave slab in strängnäs (sö 280), brate and wessén write: "the lower part of a staff, leaning slightly to the left; most likely u, possibly r". only the main staff can be seen, and the choice lies between several runes. - of a fragment in vada church, magnus källström writes in 2011: "a faintly curved branch of a k", and that the rune may also have been an f. here it is the other way round: the branch can be seen, but the main staff is gone. 2. stave means rune in old norse a written character is a stafr, plural stafir. in the eddic poem hávamál, stanza 142, the reader is advised: > rúnar munt þú finna ok ráðna stafi, mjǫk stóra stafi, mjǫk stinna stafi … > "runes you will find and readable staves, very great staves, very strong staves …" the same pair of words, runes and staves, stands on the runestones. on the nöbbele stone in småland (sm 16) the dead man is to be remembered "while the stone and the rune-staves live", meðan stæinn lifir ok stafir runa. on the randbøl stone in jutland (dr 40) it says: "very long will these staves live for þorgunnr." much later, on a medieval norwegian carving (n 13), áslakr writes: rúnar ek ríst ok ráðna stafi, "runes i carve and readable staves" – almost word for word as in hávamál. the word survives in swedish bokstav, "letter", and german buchstabe. whether the first element originally meant the book or the beech tree, which could be carved, is disputed. 3. the staves that stood beside the stones the most puzzling meaning is found on five runestones, perhaps six. there staf is not a character but a monument, raised together with the stone: - vreta in uppland (u 332): "inga raised the staff and stones in memory of ragnfastr, her husbandman." - stora rytterne in västmanland (vs 1): "guðleifr placed the staff and these stones in memory of slagvi, his son, who met his end in the east." - bällsta in uppland (u 226): "they raised the stones and worked(?) the staff also, the mighty one, as marks of honour." - balingsta in uppland (u 849): "ígull and haukr made the staff, and nasi and ônundr raised the stone." - kolsundet by husby in södermanland (sö 196): "ingifríðr had this stone and staff raised in memory of eyjulfr, her father." - fyrby in södermanland (sö 56), carved on an earth-fast boulder: the most rune-skilled brothers in middle earth "placed many a stone and staff" in memory of their father. here scholars disagree: stafa marga may also mean the runes of the text. not a single one of the staves survives. the stones have lasted a thousand years; the staves have vanished completely. that suggests they were of wood, but what they looked like, whether they were carved or painted, we do not know. the word has yet another meaning on the forsa ring in hälsingland (hs 7), an iron ring with runes from the 800s. there the fines are to be paid "to the staff". according to rundata's translation this concerns the restoration of a sanctuary. the staff is then something in law or cult, not a monument. what research says we have found little written about the staves. in her 2005 dissertation kristel zilmer divides the instances into two groups: where staf means the runes (sm 16, dr 40 and possibly sö 56) and where a staff is raised as a monument (the five above). tomáš vlasatý of projekt forlǫg has compared the staves with a contemporary eyewitness account. around the year 922 the arab envoy ibn fadlan watched a chieftain's funeral among a people he called the rus, on the volga. when the ship had been burnt, he writes, they "built something like a round hillock over the ship … and placed in the middle of it a large piece of birch on which they wrote the name of the man and the name of the king of the rūs". vlasatý suggests that wooden poles may have been a cheaper alternative to stones, lasting at most about a hundred years. that is his suggestion. but the account shows that a wooden post with writing on it could be a memorial at this time. we have not found any excavation in which such a staff was found beside a runestone. what the stones with staves have in common we compared the five stones with a certain staff with all other viking-age runestones in the scandinavian runic-text data base, fragments and lost stones included, in the statistics program r: two things stand out: - the staves stand in monuments with several stones. three of the five speak of "the staff and the stones". among all other runestones only one in thirty speaks of several stones. with five stones chance might give one hit, hardly three. the probability of so large a result by chance is 0.002, even allowing for the fact that we made seven tests. - two of the monuments belong with an assembly. at bällsta the sister stone u 225 says that the sons "made here an assembly place", and at kolsundet (sö 196) an assembly is mentioned, in an uncertain reading. among all other runestones only 9 of 2,625 mention an assembly. we saw this pattern while reading the texts, and the test was made afterwards. it is therefore a finding to be tested further, not a proof. the other differences point the same way but may be chance, since the stones are so few. the staves belong to the early part of the runestone period: three of the four with a style group are carved in rak, fp or pr1, roughly 980–1050, and the mid-year is 1030 against 1060 for the other stones in the mälaren valley (the probability of chance is 0.070, and 0.28 after adjusting for seven tests). all five stand in the mälaren valley, where three in five runestones are. two of five are signed by a carver, against about one in ten otherwise. taken together, the staves are mentioned in large, public monuments with several stones, sometimes at an assembly place and mostly early. that is what the figures show. what the staves were, we still do not know. - the 800s: the forsa ring (hs 7), staff in a legal sense. - around 980–1015 (style group rak): the runes are called staves (sm 16, dr 40), and the brothers at fyrby place "many staves" (sö 56). - around 1010–1075 (fp–pr3): staves are raised as monuments (sö 196, u 226, vs 1, u 332). - the middle ages: rúnar ek ríst ok ráðna stafi (n 13), and the prime staff on seven gotlandic inscriptions 1324–1553. 4. staveless runes on a few stones the carver has almost entirely left out the main staves. what remains are the branches and short stumps of the staff, a kind of shorthand. they are called staveless runes or, after the province where they are mostly found, hälsinge runes. the best-known example is the malsta stone in hälsingland (hs 14). they also occur in södermanland. of the aspa stone (sö 137), the swedish national heritage board's database runor notes: "the last row with staveless runes except the last word". the image at the top of the article shows the difference. in the upper rows the main staves stand as tall strokes across the whole band; in the bottom row many runes are only short slanting strokes. 5. the rune staff and the prime staff a rune staff is a calendar, usually carved on a wooden stick, where runes and signs mark the days and feasts of the year. it was used from the middle ages and in places into the 1700s. another word for it is prime staff, after the golden number, the number that gives a year's place in the nineteen-year lunar cycle and is needed to work out easter. the word is found on seven medieval inscriptions on gotland from 1324 to 1553, most of them on grave slabs: g 12, g 55, g 78, g 124, g 182, g 306, g 308. they give the year through the sunday letter and the "prime staff" in the easter table. on the slab in hemse church (g 55) from 1459, for example, it says that hagal was the sunday letter that year, and that the prime staff was the one "in the twelfth row of the table". 6. magic staves and alliteration magic staves (galdrastafir) are icelandic magical signs from manuscripts from the 1500s onwards, for example vegvísir. they are sometimes called runes, but they are signs of their own and many hundreds of years younger than the runestones. alliteration (swedish stavrim, "stave rhyme") is the rhyme of initial sounds in old norse verse: words beginning with the same sound bind the line together. the nöbbele stone's formula above is an example: meðan stæinn lifir ok stafir runa. the stone and the staves rhyme with each other. how we did it - the runestones' own words: every normalization in the scandinavian runic-text data base (version 3.1, 2018) containing staf-, with rundata's translations. words like stafn, "stem (of a ship)", are left out. - staveless runes: the notes in the swedish national heritage board's database runor (2020). - main staff and branch: the abbreviations "hst" and "bst" counted in the two parts of södermanlands runinskrifter that we have as text. the text is machine-read, so some instances may have been missed. - the statistics on the staves: the five stones with a certain staff were compared with all other viking-age runestones, fragments and lost stones included, using fisher's exact test. inscriptions on grave slabs, rock faces and loose objects such as coins and rune sticks are left out. fisher's test suits a group this small. we made seven tests, and the p-values are adjusted for that (holm's method). "several stones" means that the text has stæina, stæinar or stæinum; "assembly" that it has þing, with bällsta counted as one monument (u 225 and u 226). the assembly test was made after we had seen the pattern. the scripts are scripts/stavar data.py and scripts/stavar stats.r. - the image of the aspa stone: raking light from the north-west, computed in vitki from the open 3d scan. the images come from vitki, an open tool for runestone research that you can download and run on your own computer from github. sources - scandinavian runic-text data base (rundata), department of scandinavian languages, uppsala university. open database license. - runor, swedish national heritage board, the 2020 edition of the scandinavian runic-text data base. - brate, e. & wessén, e. 1924–36. södermanlands runinskrifter (sveriges runinskrifter 3). stockholm: kvhaa. digitised by the swedish national heritage board. - källström, m. 2011. u fv1971;212b vada kyrka. ett digitalt supplement till upplands runinskrifter, version 0.1. swedish national heritage board. - hávamál, stanza 142, in guðni jónsson's edition of the edda (heimskringla.no). the translation is ours. - ibn fadlan, risala, in james e. montgomery's translation: ibn faḍlān and the rūsiyyah. journal of arabic and islamic studies 3, 2000, pp. 1–25. - vlasatý, t. 2022. "þorbjǫrn the skald carved the runes". projekt forlǫg. - zilmer, k. 2005. "he drowned in holmr's sea – his cargo-ship drifted to the sea-bottom, only three came out alive": records and representations of baltic traffic in the viking age and the early middle ages in early nordic sources. tartu: tartu university press, p. 156. - kitzler åhfeldt, l. 2024. 3d-data runstenar i södermanland [dataset]. swedish national heritage board. doi:10.5281/zenodo.11951255. cc by 4.0.
posts.summary: ordet stav dyker upp överallt där det handlar om runor: i runologernas beskrivningar, i eddan, på runstenarna och på gamla kalendrar. det betyder minst sex olika saker. fem runstenar, och kanske ristningen vid fyrby, nämner stavar som restes bredvid stenen. ingen av dem finns kvar, men statistiken visar var de stod: i stora monument med flera stenar, ibland vid en tingsplats.
posts.summary_en: the word stave turns up wherever runes are discussed: in runologists' descriptions, in the edda, on the runestones and on old calendars. it means at least six different things. five runestones, and perhaps the carving at fyrby, mention staves raised beside the stone. none survives, but the statistics show where they stood: in large monuments with several stones, sometimes at an assembly place.

posts.title: Västgöten reste själv – upplänningen lät resa
posts.title_en: Raise It Yourself – or Have It Raised
posts.text: den som läser många runstenar märker det till slut: stenarna säger nästan samma sak, men inte med samma ord. någon reste stenen efter sin far. någon annan lät resa – och det lilla ordet lät rymmer en hel arbetsdelning: en som beställde och betalade, en annan som högg. vi har nu räknat ordvalen över hela det svenska materialet, och de visar sig varken vara slump eller smak. ordvalet följer landskapen, och det följer tiden. underlaget är de 1 848 vikingatida runstenarna i samnordisk runtextdatabas som har minst tre läsbara ord, och de 75 vanligaste orden på dem – namnen borträknade, för namn följer familjer och inte trakter. varje ord räknas en gång per sten: antingen står det där eller inte. av de orden har elva en regional signal som överlever alla kontroller vi kan utsätta den för, och trettio ändras tydligt över tid. två sätt att resa en sten uppland och västergötland gjorde samma sak med olika grammatik. på västergötlands stenar dominerar det enkla verbet: n ræisti stæin – 'n reste stenen' – står på 52 procent av stenarna, mot 10 procent i resten av landet. i uppland är samma ordform nästan utdöd, 3 procent mot 22 utanför. upplänningarna sade i stället let ræisa – 'lät resa' – och mycket riktigt står ræisa på 43 procent av upplands stenar mot 17 procent i övriga landet. skillnaden är inte bara stilistik. den som lät resa betalade någon annan för arbetet – konstruktionen bär en antydan om beställare och utförare, om en arbetsdelning som tycks ha varit självklar i mälardalen och ovanlig i väster. ingen har drivit den tanken längre än jarlabanke i täby, som inte ens väntade på att dö: "jarlabanke lät resa dessa stenar åt sig själv, medan han ännu levde ... och ensam ägde han hela täby." vi mäter orden, inte samhället bakom dem, men orden pekar. jarlabankes sten vid bron i täby en av jarlabankes stenar vid broänden i täby (u 164). texten har beställarformeln i dess mest självmedvetna form: han lät resa stenarna åt sig själv i livstiden, gærði – gjorde – bron för sin själ, and sina, och ägde ensam hela täby. tre av orden i den här artikeln på en och samma sten. att något är vanligare i ett landskap kan bero på annat än landskapet. upplandsstenarna är i genomsnitt yngre än götalands, och korta texter rymmer färre ord än långa. därför räknas varje ord i en modell som håller tiden (stilgruppens datering) och textens längd konstanta, och som dessutom behandlar ristaren som en egen källa till likhet – annars skulle en enda flitig ristares vana kunna se ut som ett helt landskaps. till sist delas varje landskaps socknar i två halvor, och signalen måste peka åt samma håll i båda. ordet som ritar en gräns kring södermanland minnesformelns lilla preposition – æftir eller at – är den skarpaste gränsen i hela materialet. på södermanlands runstenar står at på 55 procent av stenarna; i resten av landet på 19. spegelbilden: æftir står på 32 procent av sörmlandsstenarna mot 68 procent utanför. samma formel, samma betydelse – men sörmlänningarna valde det korta ordet, och grannlandskapen det långa. ordet at klarar alla kontrollerna med bred marginal: sannolikheten att se en så stor skillnad av en slump, om ordvalet egentligen vore lika i hela landet, är mindre än en på tusen biljoner. runstenen sö 14 vid gåsinge kyrka sö 14 vid gåsinge kyrka: ragna reste stenen at sven, sin make – med prepositionen som ritar södermanlands gräns. västgötarnas dräng och upplands själar två ord till som vägrar flytta hemifrån. på västergötlands stenar hyllas de döda som goðan dræng – 'en god ung man': dræng står på 12 procent av stenarna där mot 1 procent i resten av landet, och goðan på 30 mot 6. det rimmar med vad vi sett förr: västgötarnas formelspråk pekar söderut, mot det danska området, där drängarna också bor i stenarna. runstenen vg 181 vid frugården vg 181 vid frugården: gufi reste stenen – det enkla västgötska verbet – efter sonen olav, dræng harða goðan, 'en mycket god dräng', som dräptes i estland. , cc by 2.5, via wikimedia commons. titelorden þegn och drængr på kartan, med rikena omkring 1025 titelorden þegn och drængr på vitkis karta, med rikenas ungefärliga gränser omkring 1025: danmark i rött, götarnas landskap i grönt, svitjod i brunt, norge i lila. blå rutor är andelen runstenar i rutan som bär mönstret – mörkare är större andel. titlarna samlas i det danska området och i västergötland, och tunnas ut norrut mot mälardalen. kartan går att utforska själv under karta → jämför länder i appen. den här artikeln hör ihop med västgötarna skrev som danskarna. där mätte vi hur orden stavades – ljud för ljud, över riksgränsen – och västergötland lutade söderut medan gränsbygden teg. här mäter vi i stället vilka ord som alls står på stenarna, inom sverige. det är två oberoende mätningar: stavningen vet ingenting om ordvalet, och ordvalet ingenting om stavningen. att båda pekar åt samma håll – västergötland delade tradition med det danska området, och mälardalen gick sin egen väg – gör slutsatsen mycket starkare än någon av mätningarna ensam. i uppland är det i stället själen som sticker ut. bönens and – 'ande, själ' – står på 13 procent av upplands stenar mot 5 procent i övriga landet. upplands många sena, kristna stenar ber oftare för själen – och eftersom modellen håller tiden konstant är det inte bara en effekt av att uppland ristade längst. jarlabanke igen: bron gjorde han fyr and sina, för sin själ. orden som gick ur tiden trettio av de 75 orden ökar eller minskar tydligt över 1000-talet. tillsammans ser man formelboken byta skepnad. verbet gærði – 'gjorde' – står på 10 procent av de äldsta stenarna och faller till noll på de yngsta. letu – 'läto', flera beställare som lät resa – går åt andra hållet, från 5 procent till 44 som mest, och risti – 'ristade', ristarens eget verb i signaturen – växer från ingenting till 19 procent när ristarna mot slutet allt oftare skriver sitt namn. utpekandets þenna – 'denna sten' – halveras, från 29 procent till 10. dateringen förtjänar sin egen brasklapp: årtalen kommer ur ornamentikens stilgrupper, inte ur årtal på stenarna, så kurvorna beskriver stilgruppernas tid. men riktningarna håller när vi justerar för landskap och textlängd, och de berättar en begriplig historia – beställarformeln tar över, ristarna signerar, och det gamla gærði dör med sin generation. vilka landskap skriver mest lika? lägger man landskapens hela ordprofiler bredvid varandra – med korrespondensanalys, samma metod som arkeologer använder för att ordna gravfynd – hamnar södermanland och uppland närmast varandra, med östergötland strax intill. västergötland står för sig självt, draget åt sitt ræisti, sin dræng och sin goðan. det är samma bild som språkdragen gav i våra tidigare analyser, men nu framräknad ur något så enkelt som vilka ord som alls står på stenarna. orden är rundatas normaliserade former på de 1 848 vikingatida runstenarna med minst tre läsbara ord; skadade och osäkra ord räknas inte, och namn ingår inte. ett ord räknas en gång per sten. för varje ord med belägg på minst tjugo stenar skattas en logistisk modell på de 972 daterade stenarna: landskap mot riksgenomsnittet, stilgruppens mittår och textens längd som kontroller, och ristaren som slumpeffekt (stenar utan känd ristare grupperas per socken). alla p-värden justeras för de många proven (benjamini–hochberg, q under 0,05), och varje regional signal prövas dessutom i två sockenhalvor med krav på samma riktning i båda. bara östergötland, södermanland, uppland och västergötland har nog med daterade stenar för egna prov. metoden i sin helhet: methods.md, avsnitt 1m, i vitkis källkod; hela analysen går att köra om på statistiksidan i appen. vad betyder det att orden höll sig hemma? försiktigt uttryckt: att minnesformlerna inte var en rikslikare utan lokala traditioner, stabila nog att överleva justering för tid, textlängd och enskilda ristare. vad vi inte kan säga är varför – om det är dialekt i talet, formelvanor i verkstäderna eller beställarnas smak. orden skiljer inte på de tre. men gränserna de ritar är verkliga, och de går att pröva vidare: varje tabell i analysen går att ladda ner, och den som vill kan börja med att läsa en sörmländsk sten och en västgötsk bredvid varandra. lyssna efter at – och efter drängen. data: samnordisk runtextdatabas (uppsala universitet). analysen är fri programvara i vitki; alla siffror i artikeln är framräknade ur modulen ordförrådet och låsta mot dess resultat i artikelbygget. - orden på runstenarna höll sig hemma: västergötland reste sina stenar med det enkla verbet, uppland lät resa – en antydan om beställare och utförare – och södermanland satte sina märken at, inte æftir, de döda. - skillnaderna står kvar också när vi räknar bort tid, textlängd och enskilda ristare, och de håller i båda halvorna av materialet. det är lokala traditioner, inte slump. - formelboken var inte heller evig: under 1000-talet byter stenarna språkdräkt, och i själva orden syns hur beställandet och ristaryrket växer fram – letu och risti tar plats när gærði dör ut. - varför orden skiljer sig – dialekt i talet, verkstädernas vanor eller beställarnas smak – kan siffrorna inte avgöra. men gränserna de ritar är verkliga, och stavningen ritar samma gränser i en helt oberoende mätning.
posts.text_en: anyone who reads many runestones notices it eventually: the stones say nearly the same thing, but not with the same words. one man raised the stone after his father. another had it raised – and that little had holds a whole division of labour: one who commissioned and paid, another who carved. we have now counted the choices of words across the whole swedish corpus, and they turn out to be neither chance nor taste. the choice of words follows the provinces, and it follows time. the material is the 1,848 viking-age runestones in the scandinavian runic text database with at least three legible words, and the 75 most common words on them – names excluded, since names follow families rather than regions. each word is counted once per stone: either it is there or it is not. of those words, eleven carry a regional signal that survives every control we can subject it to, and thirty change clearly over time. two ways to raise a stone uppland and västergötland did the same thing with different grammar. on the stones of västergötland the simple verb dominates: n ræisti stæin – 'n raised the stone' – stands on 52 per cent of the stones, against 10 per cent in the rest of the country. in uppland the same word form is nearly extinct, 3 per cent against 22 outside. the upplanders said let ræisa – 'had raised' – instead, and accordingly ræisa stands on 43 per cent of uppland's stones against 17 per cent elsewhere. the difference is not merely stylistic. whoever had a stone raised paid someone else for the work – the construction carries a hint of commissioner and craftsman, of a division of labour that seems to have been self-evident around lake mälaren and uncommon in the west. no one took that idea further than jarlabanke of täby, who did not even wait to die: "jarlabanki had these stones raised for himself while he was still alive ... and alone he owned all of täby." we measure the words, not the society behind them, but the words point. jarlabanke's stone at the bridge in täby one of jarlabanke's stones at the bridge end in täby (u 164). the text has the commissioner formula in its most self-assured form: he had the stones raised for himself while alive, gærði – made – the bridge for his soul, and sina, and alone owned all of täby. three of the words of this article on one and the same stone. something being more common in one province can have other causes than the province. the uppland stones are on average younger than götaland's, and short texts hold fewer words than long ones. every word is therefore counted in a model that holds time (the style-group dating) and text length constant, and that moreover treats the carver as a source of similarity of its own – otherwise a single prolific carver's habit could look like a whole province's. finally, each province's parishes are split into two halves, and the signal must point the same way in both. the word that draws a line around södermanland the memorial formula's little preposition – æftir or at – is the sharpest boundary in the whole material. on the runestones of södermanland, at stands on 55 per cent of the stones; in the rest of the country on 19. the mirror image: æftir stands on 32 per cent of the södermanland stones against 68 per cent outside. the same formula, the same meaning – but the people of södermanland chose the short word, and the neighbouring provinces the long one. the word at passes all the controls with a wide margin: the probability of seeing so large a difference by chance, if the choice of words were really the same across the country, is less than one in a thousand trillion. the runestone sö 14 at gåsinge church sö 14 at gåsinge church: ragna raised the stone at sveinn, her husband – with the preposition that draws södermanland's boundary. västergötland's dræng and uppland's souls two more words that refuse to leave home. on the stones of västergötland the dead are praised as goðan dræng – 'a good young man': dræng stands on 12 per cent of the stones there against 1 per cent in the rest of the country, and goðan on 30 against 6. that fits what we have seen before: the formula language of västergötland points south, towards the danish area, where the drengs live in the stones too. the runestone vg 181 at frugården vg 181 at frugården: gufi raised the stone – the simple western verb – after his son olav, dræng harða goðan, 'a very good dreng', who was killed in estonia. the title words þegn and drængr on the map, with the realms about 1025 the title words þegn and drængr on vitki's map, with the approximate borders of the realms about 1025: denmark in red, the geatish provinces in green, svitjod in brown, norway in purple. blue cells are the share of runestones in the cell carrying the pattern – darker is a larger share. the titles gather in the danish area and in västergötland, and thin out northwards towards lake mälaren. the map can be explored under karta → jämför länder in the app. this article belongs together with the westrogothians wrote like the danes. there we measured how the words were spelled – sound by sound, across the national border – and västergötland leaned south while the border country kept silent. here we instead measure which words stand on the stones at all, within sweden. the two measurements are independent: the spelling knows nothing of the choice of words, and the choice of words nothing of the spelling. that both point the same way – västergötland shared its tradition with the danish area, and the mälaren valley went its own way – makes the conclusion far stronger than either measurement alone. in uppland it is instead the soul that stands out. the prayer's and – 'spirit, soul' – stands on 13 per cent of uppland's stones against 5 per cent elsewhere. uppland's many late, christian stones pray for the soul more often – and since the model holds time constant, this is not merely an effect of uppland carving longest. jarlabanke again: the bridge he made fyr and sina, for his soul. the words that went out of time thirty of the 75 words rise or fall clearly across the eleventh century. together they show the book of formulas changing shape. the verb gærði – 'made' – stands on 10 per cent of the oldest stones and falls to zero on the youngest. letu – 'had raised', several commissioners – goes the other way, from 5 per cent to 44 at its peak, and risti – 'carved', the carver's own verb in the signature – grows from nothing to 19 per cent as carvers towards the end sign their names ever more often. the deictic þenna – 'this stone' – is halved, from 29 per cent to 10. the dating deserves its own caveat: the years come from the ornamental style groups, not from dates on the stones, so the curves describe the style groups' time. but the directions hold when we adjust for province and text length, and they tell an intelligible story – the commissioner formula takes over, the carvers sign, and the old gærði dies with its generation. which provinces write most alike? laying the provinces' whole word profiles side by side – with correspondence analysis, the same method archaeologists use to order grave finds – södermanland and uppland end up closest to each other, with östergötland just beside them. västergötland stands on its own, pulled towards its ræisti, its dræng and its goðan. it is the same picture that the language traits gave in our earlier analyses, but now computed from something as simple as which words stand on the stones at all. the words are the normalised forms of the runic text database on the 1,848 viking-age runestones with at least three legible words; damaged and uncertain words are not counted, and names are excluded. a word is counted once per stone. for every word attested on at least twenty stones, a logistic model is fitted on the 972 dated stones: province against the national mean, the style group's mid-year and the length of the text as controls, and the carver as a random effect (stones without a known carver are grouped by parish). all p-values are adjusted for the many tests (benjamini–hochberg, q below 0.05), and every regional signal is additionally tested in two parish halves, required to point the same way in both. only östergötland, södermanland, uppland and västergötland have enough dated stones for tests of their own. the full method: methods.md, section 1m, in vitki's source code; the whole analysis can be re-run from the statistics page in the app. what does it mean that the words stayed home? put cautiously: that the memorial formulas were not a national standard but local traditions, stable enough to survive adjustment for time, text length and individual carvers. what we cannot say is why – whether it is dialect in speech, formula habits in the workshops, or the taste of the commissioners. the words do not distinguish the three. but the boundaries they draw are real, and they can be tested further: every table in the analysis can be downloaded, and anyone who likes can begin by reading one stone from södermanland and one from västergötland side by side. listen for the at – and for the dreng. data: scandinavian runic text database (uppsala university). the analysis is free software in vitki; every figure in this article is computed from the ordförrådet module and locked against its results in the article build. - the words on the runestones stayed home: västergötland raised its stones with the simple verb, uppland had them raised – a hint of commissioner and craftsman – and södermanland set its marks at, not æftir, the dead. - the differences remain when we account for time, text length and individual carvers, and they hold in both halves of the material. these are local traditions, not chance. - nor was the book of formulas eternal: across the eleventh century the stones change their wording, and in the words themselves one can watch commissioning and the carver's trade emerge – letu and risti take over as gærði dies out. - why the words differ – dialect, workshop habit or the commissioners' taste – the numbers cannot settle. but the boundaries they draw are real, and the spelling draws the same boundaries in a fully independent measurement.
posts.summary: vi räknade de vanligaste orden på sveriges vikingatida runstenar, landskap för landskap och årtionde för årtionde. orden håller sig hemma: västergötland reste sina stenar med egna händer, uppland lät andra göra jobbet, södermanland satte sina märken at – inte æftir – de döda. elva ord vägrar vara rikssvenska, och trettio byter skepnad mitt under 1000-talet.
posts.summary_en: we counted the most common words on sweden's viking-age runestones, province by province and decade by decade. the words stayed home: västergötland raised its stones with its own hands, uppland had others do the work, södermanland set its marks at – not æftir – the dead. eleven words refuse to be national, and thirty change shape in the middle of the eleventh century.

posts.title: Runorna som fattas – ett pågående arbete med Vitkis sannolikhetsmodell
posts.title_en: The missing runes – work in progress on Vitki's probability model
posts.text: sö 45 i strykljus, med närbild av de skadade runorna sö 45 vid stora släbro i södermanland, i strykljus ur en 3d-skanning. till höger det vänstra runbandet i närbild. inom den streckade ringen är två runor skadade i stenens första ord, mansnamnet gæirf[as]tr: den ena av flinta, den andra av en djup grop. bilden är beräknad i vitki ur laila kitzler åhfeldts skanning (riksantikvarieämbetet, cc by 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.11951255). nästan ingen runsten har klarat tusen år utan skador. stenar har spruckit, flisor har lossnat och vittringen har ätit sig in i ristningen. av de 2 633 vikingatida runstenarna i samnordisk runtextdatabas har 1 087 minst ett ställe där en till fyra runor har gått förlorade. när runologerna ger ut en sten fyller de ofta sådana luckor. de ifyllda runorna sätts inom hakparentes, som i gæirf[as]tr. hakparentesen säger att runorna inte syns på stenen. den säger inte hur säker utgivaren var, eller vilka andra möjligheter som vägdes. i vitki bygger vi en modell som gör samma arbete på ett annat sätt. den föreslår vad som stod i luckan, rangordnar förslagen och anger hur säker den är. procenten är prövad mot luckor där svaret är känt, så att 90 procent ska betyda att förslaget stämmer ungefär nio gånger av tio. här berättar vi hur långt vi har kommit, och vi redovisar varje prov, så att den som vill kan granska hur posts.text_en: sö 45 in raking light, with a close-up of the damaged runes sö 45 at stora släbro in södermanland, in raking light from a 3d scan. on the right, a close-up of the left rune band. inside the dashed ring two runes are damaged in the stone's first word, the man's name gæirf[as]tr: one by flint, the other by a deep pit. the image is computed in vitki from laila kitzler åhfeldt's scan (swedish national heritage board, cc by 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.11951255). hardly any runestone has survived a thousand years undamaged. stones have cracked, flakes have come off and weathering has eaten into the carving. of the 2,633 viking-age runestones in the scandinavian runic-text data base, 1,087 have at least one place where one to four runes have been lost. when runologists publish a stone they often fill such gaps. the restored runes are put in square brackets, as in gæirf[as]tr. the brackets say that the runes cannot be seen on the stone. they do not say how sure the editor was, or which other possibilities were weighed. in vitki we are building a model that does the same work in a different way. it proposes what stood in the gap, ranks the proposals and states how sure it is. the percentage is tested against gaps where the answer is known, so that 90 per cent should mean that the proposal is right about nine times out of ten. here we report how far we have come, and we account for every test, so that anyone who wishes can examine how the model is built and tested before it is released. - the model is part of vitki's open source code but is not yet released in the app. we are still testing and improving it. - the figures apply to the version we have today (textmodel-18, october 2026) and may change. - the figures apply to runestones, fragments and lost stones included. the model also reads inscriptions on other stones and loose objects such as amulets and rune bones, and where it does we say so. - the proposals are proposals, not interpretations. the model works with runes, words and word order, not with what a text means. a puzzle with too few pieces the younger futhark has only 16 runes, but the language had many more sounds. the same rune therefore had to stand for several sounds: ᚴ could be k, g or ng, and ᛁ could be i, e, æ or j. nor did the carvers always put dividers between the words. a sequence of runes can thus be read in several ways even when all the runes survive. when some are missing, the possibilities multiply. one rune – several sounds a selection from the model's spelling table, simplified. the model has learned how often each sound was written with each rune, in different periods and regions. how the model reasons take sö 45 as an example. according to södermanlands runinskrifter the stone is broken into three pieces. the first name begins with the runes kai on the lowest piece and continues with rfastr on the upper left one. there the stave of the a is "indistinct because of flint", and of the s only "the upper stave and the starting point of the middle stroke" remain; "the rest of the rune is destroyed by a deep pit". the editors read gæirf[as]tr. the model is shown the runes kairf??tr, where the two question marks are the lost runes. how the model reasons the model's steps, with the gap on sö 45 as the example. first the model tries which words can be spelled with the surviving runes plus two more. then each proposal is weighed by how well it fits where it stands. it is the same principle as when a phone suggests the next word: some words tend to follow certain others. here the word stands first in the text, followed by another name, æistfari, and the verb ræisþu, 'raised'. the name gæirfastr occurs on several other stones, for example sö 227, sm 111 and u 1144, so the model knows it. we did not enter any traces of the runes here. the answer is gæirfastr with 95 per cent and gæirfriðr with 1. the first proposal is the same name that the editors wrote in. the model has not seen the text of sö 45 itself, because a stone is always read by a version of the model that was trained without it. the building blocks the model is not one big machine but several parts, each of which can be tested on its own. several of them are well-tried methods from language technology. the model learns the language from every kind of viking-age inscription, not only the runestones, since it is the same on an amulet as on a stone. - spelling. the model has learned how sounds were written in runes from 27,218 pairs of carved words and their normalized form, from 2,877 inscriptions. spelling is estimated for each period and region, so that a stone from the 900s is not read like one from the 1000s. - word order. how often one word follows another is counted with a method from speech recognition, kneser–ney smoothing (kneser & ney 1995). it also gives rare word pairs a reasonable chance. - word classes. words that occur in similar contexts are grouped automatically. the genitives hans, hennar, sina and þæira end up in the same class without anyone having told the model what a genitive is. this helps it with rare words. the classes are computed with scikit-learn. - names. many names occur on one stone only. the model therefore builds unknown names from first elements, second elements and endings, spelled as the carvers spelled them. the first element ragn-, for example, is carved as rahn 17 times in rundata. - neighbouring stones. names on stones within ten kilometres weigh a little more, since the same families often raised several stones in the same district. - dividers. carvers differed. most put dividers between nearly all words, some between none at all. the model therefore estimates for each stone how often that carver marked a word boundary, and lets this decide how readily it places a boundary itself where the carver put no sign. - traces. if a remnant of a rune is visible in the scan or in the edition's description, it can be entered. a trace counts as likely but not certain, so that a misread remnant does not shut out the right answer. - calibration. the model's own percentages were too high, especially for names. they are therefore adjusted with a logistic model, the same principle as in platt (1999), separately for formula words, known names, names the model has composed itself and other words. all the proposals in a gap are calibrated together, and "none of the proposals" gets a probability of its own; the first choice gets a deduction of its own, since it was chosen precisely because its probability was the highest. the calibration is estimated on three kinds of gaps with a known answer, described below. - no cheating. the material is split into five parts by signum. a stone is always read by a model trained on the other four, so that the editors' restoration never leaks in. when a single stone is to be analysed, the model can also be trained on everything except that stone. six tests with a known answer a proposal is only worth something if you know how often it is right. we therefore test the model in six ways, always on stones it was not trained on. each test answers a question of its own: - the reading test: does the model read whole texts correctly when it must decide for itself where the words begin? - the masking test: can it fill runes that we hide in texts with a known answer? - the hard masking test: can it do the same when the answer is never a formula word? - the editors' gaps: does it arrive at the same word as the editors where they have filled a gap? - the documented gaps: is it right where runes have really been lost but are known from older drawings? - the dating test: can it tell when a text was written, from the language alone? the reading test. the model reads 808 inscriptions where the answer is known, 10,669 words in all, without the editors' word boundaries. it chooses the same word as the editors in 84.3 per cent of cases and divides the words correctly in
